name: github_search
description: Search GitHub as the user (their gh login on one of their machines). kind "issues" (default) finds issues and pull requests with GitHub's search syntax, e.g. "is:pr is:open review-requested:@me", "involves:@me is:open updated:>2026-01-01", "repo:owner/name label:bug"; add involves:@me unless the user asked about something wider. kind "code" searches code ("repo:owner/name symbol"). Returns one line per result with its repo#number, state, title, author, last update and URL; read one with github_read.

kind.description: issues (issues and pull requests, the default) or code

name: github_read
description: Read one GitHub pull request or issue: title, state, author, labels, the description, and for a pull request its branches, merge state, requested reviewers and reviews; then its comments, newest first (long texts are cut). Use github_diff for what a pull request changes and github_checks for its CI.

number.description: The issue or pull request number

comments.description: How many of the newest comments and reviews to include (default 15)

name: github_diff
description: What a GitHub pull request changes. Without path: every changed file with its status and lines added / removed. With path: that file's patch (cut when very long; a file too big for GitHub to show has only its counts).

path.description: One changed file's path, for its patch

name: github_checks
description: The checks (CI) of a GitHub pull request's head commit, or of a commit / branch: each check's name, status and conclusion. For failed GitHub Actions jobs it adds the last part of the job's log, where the error usually is.

number.description: A pull request number (its head commit is checked)

ref.description: A commit SHA or branch name, instead of number

name: github_comment
description: Comment on a GitHub pull request or issue as the user. Everyone who can see the repository sees it (for a public repository, everyone), so the user approves each comment on their phone before it is posted, unless their rules allow it. Write what the user would write; never post on your own initiative what they have not asked for.

number.description: The issue or pull request number

name: github_review
description: Submit a review on a GitHub pull request as the user: approve it, request changes, or comment. The user approves it on their phone first (an approval says so in bold), unless their rules allow it. Only approve when the user has said to.

event.description: APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES (body required) or COMMENT (body required)
